name: IL-16
label: Likely R

key_factors: R+11 partisan lean in a safely Republican district
Markets price LaHood at 94% to win
No public polling of the race
model.rationale: The district's R+11 lean, LaHood's incumbency and overwhelming financial edge, and prediction markets pricing him near 94% all point to a comfortable Republican hold. Nolley's modest fundraising gives him little path to close a double-digit gap.
model.watch: Any late polling showing LaHood under 55% or a surge of Democratic outside spending would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Darin LaHood seeks another term in a central Illinois district that leans Republican by about eleven points. He enters the general election with a decisive financial advantage, holding $6.7 million on hand after raising $3.7 million, while Democrat Paul Nolley has raised roughly $416,000 and has just $230,000 available. No outside groups are meaningfully engaged on either side.

No public general-election polls cover the race, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive, suggesting both sides view it as safely Republican. Prediction markets give LaHood about a 94% chance of winning. The forecast expects LaHood to prevail by roughly fifteen points, with modest uncertainty given the absence of direct polling.
